text:
tara: Observed gradual memory drift on prod-kv shard-11 since 05:20 UTC; tailed logs show repeated long-seq writes. opening this thread for postmortem follow-ups.
lee: grabbed heap dumps and jemalloc stats: gs://redwood/prof/2472209999/heap.tar.gz. early signal points to many 32-64B allocations from index encoder path.
jonathan: rolling interim mitigation: bump eviction aggressiveness for shard-11 to reduce residency while we debug. will monitor OOMs and latency.
tara: noted. that should be customer-safe for now; inform support if evictions affect throughput.
victor: i'll run a differential flamegraph (current vs baseline) and post results. linking perf harness for replication: https://perf.redwood/repro/kv-longseq-2027.
ops-bot: canary deploy "shard-evict-bump" started at 2472210050 (shards 11/20).
lee: flamegraph uploaded: gs://redwood/prof/2472209999/flame.svg. allocation stack: encoder.go:128 -> persist/encode.go:56 -> cache/entry.go:42. also see higher fragmentation % in jemalloc stats.
jonathan: proposals and owners: 1) profiling + flamegraph diffs 1 owner @lee 1 due Mon EOD; 2) soft-residency per-shard design + rollback runbook 1 owner @jonathan 1 PR by Wed; 3) buffer pooling quick patch 1 owner @victor 1 PR by tomorrow AM; 4) jemalloc tuning experiment 1 owner @lee 1 canary results by Tue.
tara: please add these to the incident action sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ghi789 and set reminders.
victor: pooling microbenchmarks show ~35% lower alloc rate on the hot path; opening branch feat/pool-idxbufs.
lee: if pooling reduces alloc churn but not residency, next step is compact cadence + targeted eviction for long sequences.
jonathan: created tickets RI-2733 (soft-residency), RI-2734 (pool-idxbufs), RI-2735 (jemalloc-tune). ops-bot attached due dates.
ops-bot: RI-2733 assigned to jonathan, due 2027-03-31.
tara: scheduling a triage on Wed 09:30 PT to review canary metrics and close actions. anyone with blockers ping me.
victor: will draft a short support blurb in case evictions impact latency.
lee: follow-up note: track seq_len distribution per-shard; recurring incidents cluster at p95 seq_len > 900. add threshold row in the sheet.
jonathan: agreed. softlimit should be percentile-driven, not global. will document rollout plan and rollback criteria in RI-2733.
tara: thanks all. we aim to close quick fixes within 72h and experimental tuning within 2 weeks. will update the postmortem with owners/dates after Wed triage.
